omissions.reason: The canceled e changes the gender of the French article une to un; both render as a before the English noun.

variant_notes.note: French résultera becomes résulte by cancellation of ra; English expresses the tense change with will result/results.
The French future ending ra is canceled; English uses will come/comes, retaining the uncertainty of the adjacent source stem in both renderings.
The canceled remainder of en termes d’un is translated as n terms of a; the uncanceled initial e remains a literal letter fragment and is explained in the translator note.
